huntBeats.text: A woman, maybe 30s, with a slouched posture spends the afternoon with the tall sunflower-like stalks with knobby tubers at the base, found in sunny patches — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. Edible, but it argues on the way down. The fire's verdict: food, carefully. Small amounts.
★ IDENTIFIED: Jerusalem Artichoke. Tall sunflower stalks; dig at the base for knobby tubers. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
💡 Jerusalem Artichoke. The tall sunflower-like stalks with knobby tubers at the base, found in sunny patches you've been looking at for days finally has a name, and now you'll never unsee it.
"The sick need tending — triage tents, broth, boiled water. Or we tighten our belts and wait it out. Or the hale hunt while the sick lie still."

👁 It is hunting you. Don't run — that invites the chase. Hold your ground, strike true, or wear the claws.
⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Ghost Trail! You read tracks so well it's almost seeing the past. Hunt finds +25%. (Your knowledge of Reading Tracks amplifies your tracker.)

Sofia leans in, voice low. "Here's what we figured out about ducks in a row. Break the line. The line is one animal, but only while it's whole. Strike a duck that ISN'T the head and the line splits — both halves hunt on their own and the formation dies. Break the line, then thin the pieces."

💡 COUNTER LEARNED — ducks in a row: Break the line. The line is one animal, but only while it's whole. Strike a duck that ISN'T the head and the line splits — both halves hunt on their own and the formation dies. Break the line, then thin the pieces. (Someone at the haven knew the trick.)
